mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding future equity value.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >50% of FEDFUNDS > 4% regimes, or FEDFUNDS volatility is below 0.5% during the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payrolls increase exceeding 50,000 jobs followed by a decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% simultaneously predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strength supports corporate optimism.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >40% of such labor strength events, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a regression with controls.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in industrial production by more than 3% coincident with a 2% drop in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates a demand shock that depresses equity valuations in the near term.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of such contraction events, or the shock is not statistically significant (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-month decline in the industrial production index below 100 (base 2017) suggests supply-side constraints that reduce future earnings expectations, driving a negative 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-negative in >60% of INDPRO < 100 periods, or the effect is not robust to rolling window tests.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 5%, it predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate looser policy and lower rates.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically outperforming the S&P 500 benchmark (IC > 0.05) in 70% of such events.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate falling below 4% without a corresponding rise in payrolls suggests a labor market tightening that raises risk premia and depresses equity valuations over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of such cooling episodes, or the effect is not significant after controlling for inflation and growth.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% signals accelerating demand, which typically precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as equities adjust to higher growth expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >55% of such inflation spikes, or the effect is not robust across multiple inflation regimes.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) both fall simultaneously by more than 2% in the same month, it indicates dual supply and cost pressures that drive a negative 5-day forward S&P 500 return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-negative in >60% of such dual declines, or the shock is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
